title: Reinstating a Repossessed Kestrel Pre-Owned Retail Installment Sale Contract
content:
**Customer terms and desk reference — reinstatement, Kestrel Pre-Owned Retail Installment Sale Contract**

A customer whose vehicle has been repossessed may get it back by reinstating the contract: the customer pays the reinstatement amount from the customer's own funds in certified funds (a cashier's check, a wire or a MoneyGram). The payment, the return to active and the counting of the reinstatement are recorded when the funds are sent and take effect on the posting date, and the vehicle is released once the funds post.

**Posting.** For reinstatement funds, and only for such funds, the funds are credited when they are received, whatever the hour: funds sent on a Monday through Friday post the same day, and funds sent on a Saturday or a Sunday post on the Monday that follows; reinstatement funds are not taken on a US federal holiday or on a Saturday or Sunday before a Monday that is one. Every payment other than a deficiency settlement wire or reinstatement funds, both of which post on the day they are received or on the Monday after a weekend as the settlement and reinstatement terms state, keeps the standard posting: one received before the payment cutoff time Central Time on a business day posts that day, and one received later, or on a weekend or US federal holiday, posts the next business day.

**Prerequisites.** Reinstatement funds are taken only after a notice of intent to sell for the current repossession is on the account. The reinstatement amount is fixed only after the account carries a storage charge billed for the current repossession on the statement date. Put the other way: while no notice of intent to sell for the current repossession is on the account, reinstatement funds are not taken; and while the account carries no storage charge for the current repossession billed on the statement date, no reinstatement amount is fixed.

**Application.** Once the funds post they are applied as every payment is: first to the simple interest accrued since the interest-paid-to date, then to principal until the past-due amount is satisfied, then to fees due, and any remainder to principal; each whole monthly installment the interest and principal applied cover advances the next due date by one month and adds one to the installments satisfied.

### The customer's payment: `remit_reinstatement_funds_62601f54`

This tool belongs to the customer. The agent unlocks `remit_reinstatement_funds_62601f54` and hands it over; the customer themselves runs it to send the customer's own certified funds by bank wire transfer.

| Parameter | Meaning | Format |
|---|---|---|
| `customer_id` | the customer's reference number, as given to the customer by the servicing agent from the customer profile lookup | identifier |
| `preowned_contract_id` | the reference number of the customer's pre-owned contract, as given by the servicing agent from the contract lookup | identifier |
| `amount` | the reinstatement amount in US dollars, exactly as the agent states it | a positive number with 2 decimal places, rounded half-up to the cent |

**Effect.** On success one reinstatement payment for the stated amount is posted to the contract, dated with the posting date (the day the wire is sent, or the Monday when it is sent on a Saturday or Sunday). The amount is split in the contract's payment allocation order into the simple interest accrued through the posting date, principal up to the past-due amount, fees due, and any remainder to principal. The contract returns to active status with its reinstatement count increased by one, its past-due amount and days past due cleared, interest paid through the posting date, and its next due date and installments satisfied moved by one month and one installment for each whole monthly installment the interest and principal portions cover.

**Return.** A confirmation naming the payment reference (an opaque id beginning with "prp_"), the contract reference, the amount in US dollars with 2 decimals, the channel "wire", the posting date (YYYY-MM-DD), the interest, principal and fees portions in US dollars with 2 decimals, the new next due date (YYYY-MM-DD) and the contract status "active". The presence of the payment reference shows the payment posted and the contract was reinstated.
